title: Latency stage entropy logbook
content:
Purpose:
This note captures an exploratory approach we sketched for detecting and triaging anomalous end-to-end latencies by computing 'stage entropy' fingerprints over traces. Goal: find systematic, recurring micro-pathologies that are not obvious in p50/p95/p99 single-metric dashboards.

Background / motivation:
- We have many existing p50/p95/p99 breakdowns per route and per model, but rare, high-impact p99 modes often come from diverse stage-order permutations (e.g., extra KV miss + rehydrate + fallback model call).
- Traditional aggregation hides multi-stage interactions. Entropy across stage residence distributions (and transitions) can highlight traces where the pattern deviates from baseline.

High-level approach:
1) Instrument each logical stage with a small enum: {receive, auth, route, kv-lookup, kv-rehydrate, compile, model-infer, postproc, send}.
2) For each trace, convert the ordered sequence of stage durations into a normalized per-stage residence vector (fractional time per stage) and a transition sequence (stage->stage).
3) Compute two metrics per trace:
   - residence_entropy: Shannon entropy of the residence vector (base-2). Low entropy means one dominant stage; high entropy means time spread across many stages.
   - transition_surprisal: KL divergence between empirical transition probabilities for this trace and baseline transition matrix for that route/model.
4) Create a 2D scatter (residence_entropy vs transition_surprisal) and overlay p50/p95/p99 buckets to find regions enriched for high-latency traces.

Sampling strategy and datasets used:
- Baseline epoch: 2025-01-15 -> 2025-01-21 (all traffic for route /generate-text, model v2.3). N=120k traces.
- Investigation window: 2025-02-10 -> 2025-02-16 (after rollout of batch-scheduling change). N=95k traces.
- We stratify by seq_len cohort: short (<128), medium (128-512), long (>512). We also stratify by coldstart flag (node_warm=false).
- Sampling: for exploratory charts we sampled 5k traces per cohort (random uniform). For targeted outlier reproduction we replayed specific traces recorded in trace-store.

Instrumentation notes (pragmatic):
- Small enum metadata emitted as tags to traces to avoid large spans. Span names left unchanged.
- Added a lightweight histogram of per-stage durations to the trace payload (proto field stage_durations_ms: list[int]). Should keep <1KB.
- Edge-case: some legacy routes don't include kv-lookup tag; treat missing as 0ms with explicit tag kv-absent.

Key charts and numbers (representative, see attached dashboards):
- Overall p50/p95/p99 for route /generate-text (investigation window, combined cohorts): p50=42ms, p95=188ms, p99=834ms.
- Region A (short seq, warm nodes): p50=28ms, p95=86ms, p99=312ms.
- Region B (long seq, warm nodes): p50=210ms, p95=434ms, p99=1.8s.
- Entropy scatter: majority of traces cluster at residence_entropy 1.2-1.8 bits and surprisal <0.8. High-latency p99 traces cluster in two lobes: low-entropy (dominant model-infer) and high-entropy/high-surprisal (multi-stage pathologies).

Representative trace fingerprints (examples):
- Trace ID: tx-20250212-7f3a91 (p99, short seq)
  - residence vector: receive:2%, auth:1%, route:5%, kv-lookup:28%, kv-rehydrate:32%, model-infer:25%, postproc:6%, send:1%
  - residence_entropy=1.65, transition_surprisal=2.1 (high)
  - Notes: KV rehydrate unusually high; correlated with s3-get retries in the same trace.

- Trace ID: tx-20250213-d19b02 (p99, long seq)
  - residence vector dominated by model-infer (82%) => low entropy 0.42; normal transitions; suggests model-side tail.
  - Action: route to model variant with more aggressive kv-cache hit prefetching.

Findings / hypotheses so far:
- After the batch-scheduler rollout (2025-02-09) we see an emergent class of p99 traces with elevated transition_surprisal. Symptoms: sporadic extra 'serialize->s3-get->kv-rehydrate' detours triggered by cache eviction churn under new batching. Hypothesis: batching increased memory pressure on node-local cache leading to higher eviction rates and more cold rehydrates.
- A second class remains classic model-side long tail (low-entropy): likely queueing/backpressure inside GPU inference process for very long sequences.

Practical triage flow (recommended):
1) Surface top 500 high transition_surprisal traces in the investigation window, grouped by node and physical host.
2) For host-buckets with >5% of these traces, inspect local cache eviction logs and dmesg for OOM/killing events.
3) Replay representative trace(s) against both pre-rollout and post-rollout configurations to confirm the delta. Use trace-replay harness: 
   - command: trace_replay --trace-id tx-20250212-7f3a91 --config pre-rollout.json
4) If repro is consistent, experiment with: increasing cache size, tuning batching threshold, or pinning small batch windows for routes heavy on kv.

Instrumentation & dashboard next steps (short list):
- Add a small 'entropy' panel to per-route latency dashboard (scatter + density contours).
- Add automated daily job: compute top-100 surprisal traces per route and create a Slack digest to #serving-runtime for triage. (owner: Aisha)
- Deploy an A/B experiment that disables new batch-scheduler for 1% of traffic for 48h to measure delta in eviction rates and surprisal counts.

Open questions / unknowns:
- We currently assume transition baselines are stationary week-to-week; how sensitive is KL-based surprisal to natural route changes (e.g., new features)? Need to compute rolling baseline.
- How to handle traces with missing stage tags (backcompat)? Currently treat as explicit zeros but that can bias entropy downward.
- Cost: stage_durations in traces increases event size. Need to validate storage and sampling rates to keep costs reasonable.

Immediate action items (owners + ETA):
- Aisha: dashboard widget prototype + Slack digest POC (ETA: 2025-02-28)
- Evan: run host-level correlation of top surprise traces -> cache eviction logs (ETA: 2025-03-05)
- Sofia: setup A/B experiment gating in rollout config (ETA: 2025-03-09)
- Marco: follow-up on replay harness improvements and produce reproducible scripts (ETA: 2025-02-25)

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider second-order metric: conditional entropy of residence vector given seq_len cohort (to normalize against predictable sequence-length effects).
- Could compress transition sequences into n-gram fingerprints (e.g., 2-gram frequency) and cluster to find recurring path motifs.
- Worth exploring a small ML classifier (random forest) to predict p99 label using residence + transition features; might auto-surface weighted feature importance for triage.

References and quick links:
- Slack: #serving-runtime thread "batching-rollout-2" (Feb 9-12)
- Trace replay tool: github.com/redwood-inference/devtools/trace-replay
- JIRA: SERV-4123 (batch-scheduler rollout rollback investigation)

Raw notes / scratch log:
- 2025-02-10 09:12: quick spike in surprisal; pinned to host ip 10.4.12.23; host had kernel OOM kill log for sidecar process (curious).
- 2025-02-11 16:03: reproduced one trace with pre-rollout config; rehydrate path absent.
- 2025-02-14 11:20: A/B gating request filed.

End of log.

(Attach: I will export the exploratory charts to confluence and link; keep this doc as living notes until we have a final RCA.)
